note: Distinct in this collection; the near neighbours are typo3-initial-release (shipping an artefact, not recording a choice) and any skill that produces documentation. Cases lead with the recurring-argument symptom that actually sends people to ADRs.

evals.prompt: We keep re-arguing the same database choice every quarter and nobody remembers why we landed where we did. How do I write that down so it stops?
evals.note: The symptom that produces ADRs, stated without the acronym.

evals.prompt: Document why we picked Redis over Memcached, including the options we rejected and what would make us revisit it.
evals.note: Single decision with alternatives and reversal conditions.

evals.prompt: Our decision log has 40 entries and about half of them contradict each other. Can you audit it?
evals.note: Audit and supersession, the maintenance half of the skill.

evals.prompt: We changed our mind about the queue system last month. How do I record that without deleting the old entry?
evals.note: Supersession specifically - the thing people get wrong by editing history.

evals.prompt: Our extension is finished. Tag 1.0.0 and prepare the TER upload.
evals.note: Shipping an artefact, not recording a choice.

evals.prompt: Set up a Kubernetes ingress for our staging cluster.
evals.note: Infrastructure task outside this collection entirely.
